summary: A project declares the commands that must pass before a human is asked to ship, as a `preShipChecks` list (name, command, optional timeout) in `.claude/delivery-policy.yaml`. `loom run` adds a second executor-internal stage, `pre-ship-checks`, between `tech-writer` and `devops-engineer` in the built-in `deliver-feature` plan — after the last reviewing/documenting stage and before the stage carrying the `confirm-ship` gate. The stage runs each configured command in order through `bash -c` at the project root with `LOOM_BASE_COMMIT` set to the run's `StartCommit`, under an explicit per-check timeout (default 10 minutes). A failing or timed-out check is a terminal stage failure — named, with its full output kept in the stage's artifact, no supervisor retry, and the run never reaches `confirm-ship`; checks after it never run. With no `preShipChecks` configured, the stage records itself SKIPPED with the reason "no preShipChecks configured" rather than COMPLETED. `loom`'s own repository gets `scripts/pre-ship-check.sh`, a shell script that reproduces CI's changed-line coverage gate (`go test ./... -coverprofile=...` then `go run ./cmd/diff-coverage --base "$LOOM_BASE_COMMIT" --profile ...`) and refuses to run with an empty `LOOM_BASE_COMMIT`. This closes the gap PR #18 exposed: every agent's tests passed and the PR was approved, but CI's own coverage gate still rejected it after `confirm-ship`, because nothing in the pipeline had run the check CI runs.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given `.claude/delivery-policy.yaml` contains a `preShipChecks` list where each entry has a `name`, a `command`, and an optional `timeout`, when the policy config loads, then `policy.LoadConfig` decodes every entry. It MUST reject an entry with no `name`, no `command`, or an unknown key with `ErrInvalidConfig` naming the entry and the offending key.
examples: `preShipChecks: [{name: coverage, command: scripts/pre-ship-check.sh}]` decodes to one PreShipCheck with the default 10-minute timeout.
`preShipChecks: [{command: scripts/x.sh}]` (no name) is rejected naming the entry by its command since it has no name to use.
`preShipChecks: [{name: coverage, command: scripts/x.sh, retries: 3}]` is rejected naming entry "coverage" and the unknown key `retries`.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Given the built-in `deliver-feature` plan, then it MUST contain an executor-internal stage with ID `pre-ship-checks` placed after `tech-writer` and before `devops-engineer` (the stage carrying the `confirm-ship` gate), so the stage runs before that gate can halt the run.

Given one or more configured `preShipChecks`, when the stage runs, then it MUST run each command in order through `bash -c`, with the working directory set to the project root, the environment variable `LOOM_BASE_COMMIT` set to the run's `StartCommit`, and an explicit timeout per check (the entry's own, or 10 minutes when the entry sets none).
Given every configured check exits 0, then the stage MUST complete, and its artifact MUST record each check's name, exit status, duration, and the last 50 lines of its output.

Given a check exits non-zero or times out, then the stage MUST fail, name the check, and keep that check's full output in the stage's artifact. The failure MUST be terminal (no supervisor retry), the run MUST NOT reach `confirm-ship`, and checks listed after the failing one MUST NOT run.
Given no `preShipChecks` are configured, then the stage MUST be recorded SKIPPED with the reason "no preShipChecks configured", and MUST NOT report COMPLETED for checks that never ran.

Given the change is complete, then `scripts/pre-ship-check.sh` MUST exist, run `go test ./... -coverprofile=<a temporary file>` followed by `go run ./cmd/diff-coverage --base "$LOOM_BASE_COMMIT" --profile <that file>`, exit non-zero when either step fails, and refuse to run when `LOOM_BASE_COMMIT` is empty.

Given the change is complete, then `go test ./internal/orchestrator/... ./internal/policy/... ./cmd/loom/...` MUST pass, every new function MUST have cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line MUST be covered as `cmd/diff-coverage` measures it, and no file outside `scope.paths` MUST change (the run's own delivery record under `docs/features/pre-ship-checks/` excepted).

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: Every pre-ship check command runs under an explicit timeout (architecture-guardrails.md #5, no custom retry/sleep loop); an entry that sets none falls back to a documented default rather than running unbounded.

threshold.metric: default per-check timeout when an entry sets none

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: A check's command output may contain secrets from the project's own environment. The stage's on-disk artifact keeps that output so a human can diagnose a failure, but anything the executor emits to telemetry (spans, traces) MUST record only the check's name, exit status and duration, never the output text (architecture-guardrails.md #9).

Pre-ship check commands come only from the project's committed `.claude/delivery-policy.yaml`, the same trust level as the project's own CI configuration, and are never read from a work order or any other source that could be external (shared/rules/memory-trust-boundary.md's provenance discipline, applied here even though delivery-policy.yaml is not a KI).

affectedComponents.reason: Add `PreShipChecks []PreShipCheck` to `Config`, add `"preShipChecks"` to `keptKeys`, and call the new strict decode step from `LoadConfig` after `checkValues`, wrapping any failure in `ErrInvalidConfig`.

New file: the `PreShipCheck{Name, Command string; Timeout time.Duration}` type, `defaultPreShipCheckTimeout = 10 * time.Minute`, and a strict per-entry YAML-node decoder (mirroring decode.go's `decodeCondition` walk) that rejects an unknown key or a missing name/command, naming the entry by its name, else its command, else its position.

New file: decode success (name/command/timeout, default timeout when omitted), and every rejection case — no name, no command, unknown key — each asserting the entry is named in the error, plus the absent-key case decoding to an empty slice.

No functional change expected — `Enabled()`'s tolerant `decodeConfig` call is unaffected since `PreShipChecks` decodes separately in `LoadConfig`. Re-run `go test ./internal/policy/...` to confirm the kill switch stays orthogonal to this feature.

Add `const PreShipChecksStageID = "pre-ship-checks"`; insert it into `DefaultDeliverFeaturePlan`'s `agents` slice between `"tech-writer"` and `"devops-engineer"`; extend the `Internal:` expression (currently `id == RouterStageID`) to also mark `PreShipChecksStageID` internal. Leave it out of `defaultSkippableStages` so it always reaches the internal dispatch (its own "nothing configured" self-skip is independent of the router).

Generalize `runInternalStage` from its current switch-of-one (router only) into a two-case dispatch keyed on `stage.ID`, per the function's own comment that a second internal stage should make this a registry. Widen its signature to accept `ctx context.Context` and `*RunState` so the new case can read `state.StartCommit` and respect cancellation.

New file: `runPreShipChecks` (loops `e.preShipChecks`, running each via `exec.CommandContext` with `bash -c <command>`, `Dir: input.ProjectRoot`, `Env` including `LOOM_BASE_COMMIT=<StartCommit>`, and a per-check `context.WithTimeout`); renders a markdown report (name, exit status, duration, last 50 lines on pass, full output on the failing check) to `<WorkspaceDir>/pre-ship-checks.md`; returns `StageOutput{Skipped:true, SkipReason:"no preShipChecks configured"}` when `e.preShipChecks` is empty, and returns the written artifact path alongside a non-nil error on the first failing or timed-out check.

New file: run the internal stage via the mock-provider harness (newHarness pattern from executor_test.go) with stub commands `true`, `false`, a `sleep` that outlives a short configured timeout, and `echo $LOOM_BASE_COMMIT` — asserting COMPLETED+artifact content on all-pass, FAILED+terminal+preserved full output+later checks never run on a non-zero exit or timeout, and SKIPPED with the exact reason string when no checks are configured.

Add `Skipped bool` and `SkipReason string` to `StageOutput`, so an internal stage can report "nothing to do" without going through the router's route-based skip (which is keyed to the analyst's typed state, not to delivery-policy.yaml).

Add an `artifactPath string` field to `stageFailure` so a failing check's full-output markdown file is still recorded as the stage's artifact (`record.ArtifactPath`/`ArtifactSHA256`) even though the stage ends FAILED, not COMPLETED. `invocationFailureClass` already returns `FailureTerminal` for `stage.Internal` stages, so no change needed there for the "no supervisor retry" requirement.

Add `preShipChecks []policy.PreShipCheck` field and `WithPreShipChecks([]policy.PreShipCheck) *Executor`. Widen `runOrInvoke`'s and `executeStage`'s calls to `runInternalStage` to pass `ctx` and `state` through. Add a `persistSkippedInternal` path inside `persistCompletion` for `output.Skipped`, writing `StageStatusSkipped` + `SkipReason` and emitting `EventStageSkipped` instead of completing normally. Thread `output.ArtifactPath` into the `stageFailure.artifactPath` built in `executeStage`'s failure branch.

Add (or extend an existing plan test) asserting `pre-ship-checks` is present, positioned between `tech-writer` and `devops-engineer`, `Internal: true`, `Gate: ""`, and `Skippable: false` in `DefaultDeliverFeaturePlan()`.

Change its return signature to `([]policy.Policy, []policy.PreShipCheck, error)` and return `config.PreShipChecks` on every path, including the `policiesEnabled: false` early return — `preShipChecks` is orthogonal to that kill switch.

Update `runRun`'s call site for `loadPolicies`'s new return value; add `preShipChecks []policy.PreShipCheck` to the `runSetup` struct; in `executeRun`, call `executor.WithPreShipChecks(setup.preShipChecks)` alongside the existing `executor.WithPolicies(setup.policies)` line.

New file, in this repo's own house style (see scripts/ci-diff-base.sh): `set -euo pipefail`; refuse with a clear message when `$LOOM_BASE_COMMIT` is empty; `go test ./... -coverprofile=$(mktemp)`; then `go run ./cmd/diff-coverage --base "$LOOM_BASE_COMMIT" --profile <that file>`, propagating either command's exit code.

edgeCases.handling: Decode to the 10-minute default rather than an unbounded run.

edgeCases.case: A preShipChecks entry has no name.
edgeCases.handling: Reject with ErrInvalidConfig, naming the entry by its command (or its position if command is also absent) since there is no name to use.

edgeCases.case: A preShipChecks entry has no command.
edgeCases.handling: Reject with ErrInvalidConfig, naming the entry by its name.

edgeCases.case: A preShipChecks entry sets an unrecognized key (e.g. retries).
edgeCases.handling: Reject with ErrInvalidConfig naming both the entry and the unknown key, matching the top-level keptKeys/removedKeys discipline Config already has.

edgeCases.case: No preShipChecks key is present at all.
edgeCases.handling: Config.PreShipChecks decodes to an empty slice; the stage records itself SKIPPED with reason "no preShipChecks configured", never COMPLETED.

edgeCases.case: The first check passes and the second fails.
edgeCases.handling: The stage's artifact records the first check with its last 50 lines, the second with its full output and non-zero exit; the stage fails naming the second check; any checks after it never run.

edgeCases.case: A check hangs past its configured or default timeout.
edgeCases.handling: The per-check context deadline kills the process; the stage fails naming the check as timed out, with the classification terminal (no supervisor retry).

edgeCases.case: LOOM_BASE_COMMIT would be empty (e.g. no commits, no work tree) when the stage runs.
edgeCases.handling: The executor always sets the environment variable (to the run's StartCommit, which may itself be empty per executor.go's startCommit() comment on an absent work tree); scripts/pre-ship-check.sh carries its own independent guard and refuses to run when it receives an empty value, regardless of what the executor passed.
preShipChecks still run — that kill switch only gates .policy.yaml gate-automation evaluation (ADR-010), not this feature, which is read from the same Config but is orthogonal to PoliciesEvaluated().

edgeCases.case: pre-ship-checks fails on a resumed run.
edgeCases.handling: Same terminal-failure semantics as any other FAILED stage: a human fixes the underlying check or code and resumes; this is not loom's own bounded contract-retry loop (that is explicitly out of scope, roadmap L2.18).

scripts/pre-ship-check.sh is executable, refuses an empty LOOM_BASE_COMMIT, and reproduces CI's own diff-coverage invocation exactly.

code-reviewer and security-reviewer have both passed (this stage executes arbitrary project-declared shell commands via bash -c, which is a trust-boundary-relevant change even though the commands themselves come only from committed, CI-equivalent-trust configuration).
openQuestions: Whether the stage's own artifact is typed state or markdown. Assumption adopted: markdown (a new pre-ship-checks.md, rendered directly by the executor, not through the typed-state pipeline), since nothing downstream decodes it — matching the router's own route.md precedent and the spec's stated assumption.

What YAML shape a per-entry timeout takes. Assumption adopted: a Go duration string (e.g. "10m", "90s") parsed with time.ParseDuration, consistent with how defaultStageTimeout and other durations are already expressed in this codebase, rather than a bare integer whose unit would be ambiguous.

Whether the existing Stage.Timeout field (currently unused by any Internal stage) should bound the whole pre-ship-checks stage in addition to each check's own timeout. Assumption adopted: no — leave Stage.Timeout unused for this stage as it already is for the router, and let each policy.PreShipCheck.Timeout be the only bound, since the stage itself makes no single external call for a stage-level timeout to wrap.
